To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the heat treatment of the hybrid membrane is a critical step for controlling its pervaporation separation performance.

the free volume of the PVA/MA–TEOS hybrid membrane decreased with increasing heat treatment time or temperature, and the water flux and salt rejection increased with increasing heat treatment temperature or time.

the heat treatment of the hybrid PVA/TEOS/MA membranes has a significant effect on the membrane structure, water diffusivity and salt transport properties, which in turn affect the pervaporation separation of the aqueous salt solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of heat treatment on the pervaporation separation of NaCl aqueous solution using a hybrid PVA/TEOS/MA membrane.
the effect of heat treatment on the morphology of the PVA/MA-TEOS hybrid membrane and its separation performance for aqueous salt solution.
the effect of heat treatment on the structure of PVA/MA hybrid membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the free volume of the PVA/MA hybrid membrane is an important factor in determining the pervaporation performance of aqueous NaCl solution.
the pervaporation performance of the membrane was strongly affected by the free volume, water uptake, and salt transport properties, which were all influenced by the heat treatment.
heat treatment is an important factor to control the morphology and properties in hybrid organic-inorganic membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the salt rejection of hybrid membrane could be increased by increasing the heating temperature or time.
the heat treatment is an effective way to improve the separation performance of the PVA/MA hybrid membranes by reducing the fractional free volume and the salt transport properties.
the salt transport properties and water diffusivities were the main factors that influenced the separation performance of the hybrid PVA/ MA/TEOS membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hybrid membrane with a higher salt rejection and a lower flux can be achieved via the heat treatment process.
the heat treatment of PVA-based hybrid membranes can be optimised by balancing the water flux and salt rejection.
the hybrid PVA/TEOS/MA membrane can be used to separate aqueous salt solution with high salt rejection (99%) and high water flux (2.0–3.0 kg m−2 h−1) at room temperature.
